cohort: 743 parents of premature infants in nine different NICUs located in governmental hospitals across various locations in Egypt.
finding: High overall stress levels were reported by about three-quarters of the parents, with factors like premature infants connected to mechanical ventilators, previous neonatal death, parents living far from hospitals, infants delivered through cesarean section, insufficient income, and prolonged hospitalization beyond 5 days contributing to increased stress.
mod_finding: Parents of infants delivered through cesarean section experienced higher stress levels.
